# Notification Exporter

| Status        |           |
| ------------- |-----------|
| Stability     | [development]: logs   |
| Distributions | []        |

[development]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#development
<!-- end autogenerated section -->

Renders each log record through a user-defined [Go `text/template`](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) and
delivers the result as the body of an HTTP request to an arbitrary endpoint — Slack incoming webhooks,
Discord webhooks, PagerDuty, or any other webhook-shaped destination. Supports **logs only**.

This exporter intentionally does *not* implement its own routing/filtering DSL beyond a single optional
OTTL condition. The expected pipeline shape is:

```
receivers -> filter processor -> transform processor -> routing connector -> notification exporter (one per destination)
```

i.e. use `filter`/`transform` processors and a `routing` connector upstream to decide *what* reaches this
exporter and to shape the data; use this exporter only to render the final payload and deliver it.

## Configuration

| Field                 | Type   | Default | Description |
| ---                   | ---    | ---     | --- |
| `endpoint`             | string | (none, required) | Destination URL. Inherited from [`confighttp.ClientConfig`](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/collector/config/confighttp#ClientConfig); `headers`, `tls`, `auth`, `compression`, etc. are all available the same way. |
| `method`               | string | `POST`  | HTTP method used to deliver the notification. One of `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`. |
| `body_template`        | string | (none)  | Inline Go `text/template` source for the request body. Exactly one of `body_template` / `body_template_file` must be set. |
| `body_template_file`   | string | (none)  | Path to a file containing the template source, as an alternative to `body_template`. |
| `condition`            | string | (none)  | Optional OTTL boolean condition (same syntax as `filterprocessor`'s `log_record` conditions). Records that don't match are skipped by this exporter. When unset, every record matches. Intended as defense-in-depth for standalone use — routing normally belongs upstream in a `routing` connector. |
| `sending_queue`        |        |         | See [exporterhelper queue/retry docs](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/README.md). |
| `retry_on_failure`     |        |         | See same. |

### Template data

The body template is executed once per matched log record, against:

| Field                 | Type                | Description |
| ---                   | ---                 | --- |
| `.Body`                | `string`            | String form of the log record body. |
| `.SeverityText`        | `string`            | |
| `.SeverityNumber`      | `int32`             | |
| `.Timestamp`           | `time.Time`         | |
| `.Attributes`          | `map[string]any`    | Log record attributes. |
| `.ResourceAttributes`  | `map[string]any`    | Resource attributes. |
| `.ScopeAttributes`     | `map[string]any`    | Instrumentation scope attributes. |

### Template functions

| Function       | Signature                                  | Description |
| ---            | ---                                         | --- |
| `toJson`        | `func(v any) (string, error)`              | Marshals `v` with `encoding/json`. **Use this for every value interpolated into a JSON body** — see warning below. |
| `toJsonIndent`  | `func(v any, prefix, indent string) (string, error)` | Same, pretty-printed. |
| `join`          | `func(elems []string, sep string) string`  | `strings.Join`. |
| `lower`         | `func(s string) string`                    | `strings.ToLower`. |
| `upper`         | `func(s string) string`                    | `strings.ToUpper`. |

> **Do NOT interpolate raw strings into a JSON template. Always pipe through `toJson`.**
>
> `.Body`, `.Attributes` values, and friends come from free-text log messages — arbitrary text from
> Kubernetes controllers, applications, etc. — that can contain quotes, newlines, and backslashes. Writing
>
> ```
> {"text": "{{ .Body }}"}
> ```
>
> produces invalid JSON the moment that text contains a `"` or a newline. Write this instead:
>
> ```
> {"text": {{ .Body | toJson }}}
> ```
>
> `toJson` on a string value produces a properly quoted-and-escaped JSON string literal (including the
> surrounding quotes), so no extra `"..."` should be added around it in the template. On a map/slice value it
> produces a JSON literal that can be embedded directly in the body.

## Example: Slack incoming webhook

```yaml
exporters:
  notification/slack-warning:
    endpoint: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
    condition: severity_text == "Warning"
    body_template: |
      {"text": {{ printf "[%s] %s: %s" (index .ResourceAttributes "k8s.namespace.name") (index .Attributes "k8s.event.reason") .Body | toJson }}}
```

## Example: generic webhook with a template file

```yaml
exporters:
  notification/generic:
    endpoint: https://example.com/hooks/otel
    headers:
      authorization: Bearer ${env:WEBHOOK_TOKEN}
    body_template_file: /etc/otelcol/templates/generic.tmpl
```

## Partial failures

Delivery is attempted independently per log record. If some records in a batch fail (non-2xx response,
network error, etc.) while others succeed, only the failed records are reported back for retry/queueing —
successfully delivered records are not resent.
